text: If the Bowler toss the Ball over the Striker's Head, or bowl it so wide that it shall be out of Distance to be played at, the umpire (either with or without an Appeal from the Party receiving the innings) shall adjudge one Run to the striker, even although he attempt to hit it; which shall be put down to the Byes: and such Ball shall not be reckoned as any of the four Balls.

text: If the Bowler bowl a "No Ball" the striker may play at it, and be allowed all the Runs he can get; and shall not be put out, except by running out.

text: Or, if in striking, or at any other time while the Ball shall be in Play, both his Feet be over the Popping crease, and his Wicket put down except his Bat be grounded within it.

text: Or, if in striking at the Ball he hit down his wicket.

text: Or, if under Pretence of running or otherwise, either of the strikers prevent a Ball from being caught, the striker of the Ball is out.

text: Or, if the Ball be struck, and he wilfully strike it again. or, if in running the wicket be struck down by a Throw, or by the Hand, or Arm (with Ball in Hand) before his Foot, Hand, or Bat be grounded over the Popping crease.

text: Or, if with any Part of his Person he stop the Ball, which in the opinion of the Umpire at the Bowler's Wicket shall have been delivered in a straight line to the Striker's Wicket, and would have hit it.

text: If the players have crossed each other he that runs for the Wicket which is put down is out.

text: When a Ball shall be caught no run shall be reckoned.
text_norm: when a ball shall be caught no run shall be reckoned.

text: When a Striker shall be run out the Run which they were attempting shall not be reckoned.
text_norm: when a striker shall be run out the run which they were attempting shall not be reckoned.

text: If a lost Ball shall be called the striker shall be allowed six Runs; but if more then six shall have been run before lost ball shall have been called, then the Striker shall have all which have been run.
text_norm: if a lost ball shall be called the striker shall be allowed six runs; but if more then six shall have been run before lost ball shall have been called, then the striker shall have all which have been run.

text: When the Ball has been in the Bowler's, or Wicket Keeper's Hands it is considered as no longer in Play; and the Strikers need not keep within their Ground till the umpire has called "Play"; but if the Player go out of his Ground with an intent to run before the ball be delivered the Bowler may put him out.

text: If the striker be hurt he may retire from his Wicket, and return to it at any time in that innings.

text: If a striker be hurt some other person may be allowed to stand out for him, but not to go in.

text: No Substitute in the field shall be allowed to bowl, keep Wicket, stand at the point, or middle Wicket, or stop behind to a fast Bowler, unless with the Consent of the adverse party.

text: The umpires shall enforce this Law.

text: If any Person stop the Ball with his Bat the Ball shall be considered as dead, and the opposite Party shall add five Runs to their score; if any be run, they shall have five in all.
text_norm: if any person stop the ball with his bat the ball shall be considered as dead, and the opposite party shall add five runs to their score; if any be run, they shall have five in all.

text: If the Ball be struck the striker may guard his Wicket either with his Bat, or his Body.

text: are sole judges of fair, and unfair Play; and all Disputes shall be determined by them, each at his own Wicket; but in case of a Catch which the Umpire at the Wicket bowled from cannot see sufficiently to decide upon, he may apply to the other umpire; whose opinion is conclusive.

text: The umpires in all Matches shall pitch fair Wickets, and the Parties shall toss for the Choice of innings.
text_norm: the umpires in all matches shall pitch fair wickets, and the parties shall toss for the choice of innings.

text: They shall allow two Minutes for each man to come in, and fifteen Minutes between each innings: when the Umpires shall call "Play”, the Party refusing to play shall lose the Match.

text: They are not to order a player out, unless appealed to by the Adversaries.
text_norm: they are not to order a player out, unless appealed to by the adversaries.

text: But if the Bowler's Foot be not behind the Bowling crease, (within the return crease) when he shall deliver the Ball they must, unasked, call "no Ball".
text_norm: but if the bowler's foot be not behind the bowling crease, (within the return crease) when he shall deliver the ball they must, unasked, call "no ball".

text: If the Striker run a short run the umpire must call "One Short".

text: The Umpires are not to be changed during the Match, but by the consent of both parties.
text_norm: the umpires are not to be changed during the match, but by the consent of both parties.

text: When there shall be less than five players on a Side, Bounds shall be placed twenty-two yards each in a Line from the Off, and Leg stump.
text_norm: when there shall be less than five players on a side, bounds shall be placed twenty-two yards each in a line from the off, and leg stump.

text: must be hit before the Bounds to entitle the Striker to a Run; which Run cannot be obtained unless he touch the Bowling stump (Or Crease in a line with it) with his Bat, or some Part of his Person; or go beyond them; returning to the popping crease as at double Wicket according to the 22nd Law.

text: When the striker shall hit the Ball, one of his Feet must be on the Ground, and behind the popping crease; otherwise the umpire shall call "No Hit".

text: When there shall be less than five players on a Side neither Byes, nor Overthrows shall be allowed; nor shall the striker be caught out behind wicket, nor stumped out.
text_norm: when there shall be less than five players on a side neither byes, nor overthrows shall be allowed; nor shall the striker be caught out behind wicket, nor stumped out.

text: The field’s Man must return the Ball so that it shall cross the Play between the Wicket and the Bowling stump, or between the Bowling stump, and the Bounds; the Striker may run till the Ball shall be so returned.
text_norm: the field's man must return the ball so that it shall cross the play between the wicket and the bowling stump, or between the bowling stump, and the bounds; the striker may run till the ball shall be so returned.

text: After the striker shall have made one Run, if he start again he must touch the Bowling stump, and turn before the Ball shall cross the Play to entitle him to another.
text_norm: after the striker shall have made one run, if he start again he must touch the bowling stump, and turn before the ball shall cross the play to entitle him to another.

text: The striker shall be entitled to three Runs for lost Ball, and the same Number for Ball stopped with Hat; with Reference to the 29th, and 34th Law at double Wicket.
text_norm: the striker shall be entitled to three runs for lost ball, and the same number for ball stopped with hat; with reference to the 29th, and 34th law at double wicket.

text: When there shall be more than four Players on a side there shall be no Bounds.
text_norm: when there shall be more than four players on a side there shall be no bounds.

text: All Hits, Byes, and Overthrows shall then be allowed.
text_norm: all hits, byes, and overthrows shall then be allowed.

text: The Bowler is subject to the same Laws as at double wicket.
text_norm: the bowler is subject to the same laws as at double wicket.

text: Not more than one Minute shall be allowed between each Ball.
text_norm: not more than one minute shall be allowed between each ball.

text: If the Runs of one Player be laid against those of another the Bets depend on the first innings, unless otherwise specified.
text_norm: if the runs of one player be laid against those of another the bets depend on the first innings, unless otherwise specified.

text: If the Bets be made upon both innings, and one Party beat the other in one innings the Runs in the first innings shall determine the Bet.
text_norm: if the bets be made upon both innings, and one party beat the other in one innings the runs in the first innings shall determine the bet.

text: But if the other Party go in a second Time, then the Bet must be determined by the Number on the score
